short_role: One-way-attack uncrewed surface vessel that has forced a conventional navy back from an entire sea, without a comparable fleet of its own.
characteristics: Low-profile, high-speed hull, remotely piloted via satellite link well beyond radio horizon
~350 kg payload — enough to critically damage or sink a corvette or landing ship
Reportedly credited with damage to 18 Russian Navy vessels over the war, several with irreversible losses
Estimated $500M+ in cumulative damage to the Black Sea Fleet at a unit cost in the low hundreds of thousands
employment_notes: Operated from Ukrainian-controlled coastline against a fleet with no comparable force to counter it at sea — the fight has been waged almost entirely with shore-based missiles, USVs and drones rather than a rival navy, because the side without a fleet built an asymmetric answer instead of trying to build one.
contrast_vs_traditional: Naval power used to mean a battle fleet contesting another battle fleet. A country with essentially no traditional navy used cheap, remotely piloted attack boats to sink and damage enough of a full-sized fleet that it was pushed out of the western Black Sea and ultimately forced to relocate its remaining ships further east — the same 'expensive asset can't survive near a cheap persistent threat' logic driving tank and aircraft losses elsewhere on this battlefield, applied at sea.

reactive_behavior.description: On select: USV accelerates toward a point target, brief impact vignette.

notable_events.title: First uncrewed surface vessel to sink a warship in combat
notable_events.description: A Magura V5 swarm attack sank the Russian patrol ship Sergey Kotov in the Black Sea near Kerch Strait — the first confirmed sinking of a crewed warship by an uncrewed surface vessel in naval history.
